title: Powers of the specified rational compact-support Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $K_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ have reductions in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ for $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $K_E$ be its rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and let $\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\to K_E$ be any morphism. Use exactly the rationalized pullbacks, compact-support functor, composition identifications and direct base-change transports $B_{m,M}:R\Gamma_c(X,M)\to R\Gamma_c(X,L(g_\gamma^m)^*M)$ specified in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], not independently chosen isomorphisms. Write $G=Lg_\gamma^*$ and identify $G^m$ with $L(g_\gamma^m)^*$ by those composition maps. Then $B_{1,-}:R\Gamma_c\Rightarrow R\Gamma_c\circ G$ is natural for rational morphisms and
$$B_{m+1,M}=B_{1,G^mM}\circ B_{m,M}\qquad(m\ge1).$$
For the iterates $\varphi_E^{[m]}=\varphi_E\circ G(\varphi_E)\circ\cdots\circ G^{m-1}(\varphi_E)$, the specified global operators satisfy
$$F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ B_{m,K_E}=(F_{c,K_E}^{\,1})^m\qquad(m\ge1).$$
No invertibility or integral Weil structure on $\varphi_E$ is required.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: naturality and composition of the rationalized base-change transports and the displayed global power identity

proof.text: Write $P_r=L(g_\gamma^r)^*$. By [lem-trf-integral-compact-transport-recurrence], applied to an integral representative $M_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ of an arbitrary object $M$ of $D^b_c(X,E)$ (the objects of the two categories are the same, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]), the levelwise direct transports $\tau^{(r)}_{c,M_n}$ of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition] form morphisms of the coherent reduction towers, natural in $M_{\mathcal O}$. The recurrence of that finite-level lemma holds there as an equality of tower morphisms. Their realizations $V_{r,M_{\mathcal O}}$ therefore satisfy, integrally, $V_{m+1,M_{\mathcal O}}=R\Gamma_c(X,c_{m})\circ V_{1,P_mM_{\mathcal O}}\circ V_{m,M_{\mathcal O}}$. The same lemma identifies $V_{1}$ with the integral transport $\tau_c$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and $V_{r}$ with the integral base-change isomorphism $g^{r,*}_{\gamma,c}$. [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] states that its stage-$E$ transports $B_{r,-}$ are the rationalizations of these. By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] the stage-$E$ functors $R\Gamma_c$, $P_r$ and the comparisons $c_m$ are the unique $E$-linear extensions of the integral ones. That proposition also extends the natural transformations $V_r$ uniquely, with components $V_{r,M_{\mathcal O}}\otimes1=B_{r,M}$. Since extension is a functor, it preserves composition, and the integral identity gives $B_{m+1,M}=B_{1,G^mM}\circ B_{m,M}$ under the identification of $G^m$ with $P_m$ by the composition maps. The recurrence is proved before rationalization; scalar extension only transports it. Naturality of $B_{1,-}$ for rational morphisms is the extended naturality of $\tau_c$, which is natural in $M_{\mathcal O}$ by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport].

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: naturality and composition of the rationalized base-change transports

proof.text: Set $G=Lg_\gamma^*$, $C=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ and $t=B_{1,-}:C\Rightarrow C\circ G$. The morphism $\varphi_E:GK_E\to K_E$ and its iterates are exactly the $G$-algebra data and the maps $\varphi_E^{[m]}$ in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. By the generic transport-power lemma [lem-trf-global-frobenius-iterate-formula], the endomorphism $F=C(\varphi_E)\circ t_{K_E}$ satisfies $F^m=C(\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ t_{K_E}^{[m]}$, where $t_{K_E}^{[m]}$ is the successive composite of the degree-one transports.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: apply the transport-power identity to the rationalized compact-support functor

proof.text: The recurrence from Step 1 identifies the successive composite $t_{G^{m-1}K_E}\circ\cdots\circ t_{K_E}$ with the direct transport $B_{m,K_E}$ by induction on $m$: the base case is $B_{1,K_E}=t_{K_E}$, and the successor case is exactly $B_{m+1,K_E}=B_{1,G^mK_E}\circ B_{m,K_E}$. Substituting this identification into the equality of Step 2 gives $F^m=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi_E^{[m]})\circ B_{m,K_E}$. By the operator formula in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], this composite is the specified $F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}$, while $F=F_{c,K_E}^{\,1}$; therefore $F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=(F_{c,K_E}^{\,1})^m$.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: identify the iterated transport with B_m and conclude the displayed global power identity

proof.text: The generic transport-power lemma requires neither $\varphi_E$ nor the transport maps to be invertible. Thus the argument applies to the arbitrary morphism allowed in the statement, and no integral Weil structure or invertibility on a lattice has been introduced.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: no integrality or invertibility assumption is used

proof_origin.place: Step 1, Global powers: expands the naturality, rationalization, transport recurrence and application of the generic transport-power identity

split_report.summary: Repaired the global powers split by adding lem-trf-integral-compact-transport-recurrence. The new lemma explicitly assembles the specified finite-level transports into coherent reduction-tower morphisms, proves the recurrence as an equality of tower maps before derived realization, and only then realizes it integrally. Step 1 now tensors that established integral identity to the rational stage using the specified rationalized transports; the generic power calculation and arbitrary-morphism conclusion remain unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Step 1 (Global powers) of thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md: rationalized transport naturality and composition, the transport-power calculation, identification with B_m, and the no-invertibility clause.

tool_uses.why: Its statement supplies unique rational extension of the integral functors and natural transformations, needed only after the integral recurrence is established.
